
Main-v9: the bench's instruction card was written by a separate writer from practice examples and judged by the same rules before these rounds; it is fixed for this step, reaches this bench only, and is shown in card followed by the fixed format block. Procedures must add what the card cannot do (computed, situation-specific checks and state), never restate it. You may propose a content segment (fixed text plus a predicate over public task structure) or a computational procedure. The card and the format block are fixed and cannot be edited by you. Never route by benchmark name, task id, private path, answer or score. Use before_call to deliver segment text (and alf_before_step for action episodes); emitting the note is required to count its effect. Segment notes are at most 1500 characters and share unchanged total note caps. Confirmation and acceptance also enforce the registered cross-benchmark no-harm gate; harmful cross-firing is narrowed and rechecked or rejected. Coverage must report segments as well as procedures. Keep the existing JSON change schema: kind=new or revision (with revises for a revision), description, hooks, max_note_chars<=1500, requests_second_call=false, state_bytes=0, and replay_tests when required. In the accompanying Python module declare V222_SEGMENT='instruction-segments-v2-22', SEGMENT_HOME as the home benchmark, SEGMENT_TEXT as the complete fixed text, and SEGMENT_FIELDS as {'facts': [contiguous pieces of SEGMENT_TEXT, each <=200 characters]}. Define applies(view) using only public structural fields; before_call(view,state) must only return SEGMENT_FIELDS. For action tasks, also declare alf_before_step and return {'fields': SEGMENT_FIELDS, 'discourage': []}. No new edit kind is needed.

Coverage does not outrank a complete solution: when an item's whole answer can be computed and verified from its public input, propose that program first and keep repairing it across rounds, even at low coverage. A note that does not settle the answer leaves the answering model to re-solve, so its fixed and broken counts may only measure re-run noise; do not treat a near miss from such a note as progress.
